issue: IDOR: getOrderById has no ownership/admin check — any authenticated user can read any order (PII, shipping address, email, payment result) by guessing/iterating the order _id
evidence: const order = await Order.findById(req.params.id).populate('user', 'name email')  // route: router.route('/:id').get(protect, getOrderById)
recommendation: After fetching, verify order.user.equals(req.user._id) || req.user.isAdmin; otherwise respond 403/404. Do not rely on protect alone.

issue: IDOR + client-trusted payment: updateOrderToPaid lets any authenticated user mark ANY order as paid (no ownership check) using attacker-supplied paymentResult; no server-side PayPal capture verification
evidence: order.isPaid = true; order.paymentResult = { id: req.body.id, status: req.body.status, ... }  // route: router.route('/:id/pay').put(protect, updateOrderToPaid)
recommendation: Verify order ownership, and verify the payment server-side against PayPal's capture API before setting isPaid (ADR-0002 acknowledges the trust gap — treat as known risk and remediate).

issue: Login endpoint has no rate limiting / brute-force protection, enabling credential stuffing and password brute-force against /api/users/login
recommendation: Add express-rate-limit (e.g. 5 attempts / 15 min per IP+email) on /login and /users register; add account lockout/backoff.

issue: jsonwebtoken ^8.5.1 has known HIGH CVEs incl. signature validation bypass via insecure default algorithm in jwt.verify (GHSA-qwph-4952-7xr6) and RSA->HMAC key confusion (GHSA-hjrf-2m68-5959)
evidence: "jsonwebtoken": "^8.5.1"  (npm audit: jsonwebtoken <=8.5.1, Severity: high; jwt.verify in authMiddleware.js does not pin algorithms)
recommendation: Upgrade to jsonwebtoken@9+ and explicitly pass { algorithms: ['HS256'] } to jwt.verify to prevent algorithm confusion.

issue: Multiple outdated deps with HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs: multer <=2.1.0 (DoS), mongoose <=6.13.8 (incl. a critical advisory), express <=4.21 chain (body-parser/qs/path-to-regexp ReDoS & DoS). npm audit reports 2 critical, 20 high, 11 moderate, 6 low
recommendation: Run npm audit fix; upgrade multer@2, mongoose@7+, express@4.21+; add Dependabot/CI audit gate.

issue: Upload endpoint POST /api/upload is completely public — no protect/admin middleware. Anyone can upload files to the server's uploads/ directory, which is then served statically
evidence: router.post('/', upload.single('image'), (req, res) => { res.send(`/${req.file.path}`) })  // no protect/admin
recommendation: Require protect + admin on the upload route (only admins create/edit products).

issue: Multer config has no fileSize/file count limit — unbounded uploads enable disk-exhaustion DoS. MIME/extension check is weak (client-controlled mimetype and extension only; no magic-byte validation)
evidence: const upload = multer({ storage, fileFilter: ... })  // no limits: { fileSize }; checkFileType trusts file.mimetype and path.extname
recommendation: Add limits: { fileSize: 1-2MB, files: 1 }; validate real content type via magic bytes; randomize stored filenames; store outside web root or via object storage.

issue: NoSQL operator injection risk: req.body fields (email) passed directly into Mongoose queries with no type coercion. If a JSON object like {"$gt":""} is sent for email, it becomes a query operator (auth bypass / enumeration vectors)
evidence: const { email, password } = req.body; const user = await User.findOne({ email })
recommendation: Add express-mongo-sanitize globally and/or coerce/validate inputs (typeof email === 'string') with Joi/Zod before querying.

issue: Untrusted text (user query -> OpenAI embedding -> joined into a Postgres vector literal string) is interpolated into a SQL fragment via string concatenation. While numbers from the embedding API are normally safe, building the vector literal by string-join and passing $1::vector is fragile; more importantly the RAG flow is exposed to prompt-injection from indexed documents whose content is returned to the calling LLM
evidence: const embeddingStr = "[" + embedding.join(",") + "]"; ... await client.query(sql, [embeddingStr, top_k])
recommendation: Keep using parameterized queries (already $1/$2 — good). Additionally treat retrieved chunk text as untrusted in the agent (wrap/escape, do not let document content issue tool calls) to mitigate prompt injection; validate embedding is a numeric array before formatting.

issue: Hardcoded default Postgres credentials (proshop/proshop) as fallback in source; same weak default reused in docker-compose. Weak default creds become real creds if env not set, and the password is committed in cleartext
recommendation: Fail fast if POSTGRES_PASSWORD is unset instead of defaulting; never ship a default DB password; require strong generated secrets.

issue: Postgres uses weak default credentials and exposes port 5432 to the host; pgvector DB reachable with proshop/proshop default if env not overridden
recommendation: Require strong POSTGRES_PASSWORD (no default), and do not publish 5432 to the host unless needed; bind to internal network only.

issue: Full JWT verification error object logged via console.error on every failed auth — can leak token/JWT internals and create noisy logs; also no structured security audit logging for auth failures
owasp: A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
recommendation: Log a sanitized message (no token), emit structured audit events for repeated auth failures; avoid dumping the raw error.

issue: No server-side input validation or password strength policy on registration/profile update. Empty/weak passwords accepted; email format unvalidated; relies only on Mongoose required:true
evidence: const { name, email, password } = req.body; await User.create({ name, email, password })
recommendation: Add Joi/Zod/express-validator: enforce email format, min password length/complexity, trim/normalize before DB write.

issue: express.json() has no body size limit — large JSON payloads (e.g. order with huge orderItems array) can cause memory/CPU DoS. No helmet security headers and no global rate limiter on the API
evidence: app.use(express.json())  // no { limit }; no helmet; no express-rate-limit
recommendation: app.use(express.json({ limit: '10kb' })); add helmet() for security headers; add a global rate limiter.

issue: JWT lifetime is 30 days with no refresh/rotation/revocation and token stored in localStorage (per ADR-0001), which is XSS-exfiltratable; no algorithm pinning on sign
recommendation: Shorten access-token TTL (e.g. 15m-1h) + refresh token in httpOnly cookie; or accept documented localStorage risk (ADR-0001) and add CSP/short TTL to reduce theft window.

issue: bcrypt cost factor fixed at 10. Acceptable but below current OWASP recommendation; also pre-save hook does not return next() after hashing (functionally ok here since it's the last statement, but flagged in copilot-instructions as a double-hash hazard if edited)
evidence: const salt = await bcrypt.genSalt(10); this.password = await bcrypt.hash(this.password, salt)
recommendation: Raise bcrypt cost to >=12 (or migrate to argon2id); ensure pre-save hook explicitly returns to avoid future double-hash regressions.

issue: PayPal client id served from an unauthenticated endpoint and no CORS policy configured anywhere; default Express CORS behavior plus no helmet means missing security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.)
evidence: app.get('/api/config/paypal', (req, res) => res.send(process.env.PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID))  // no cors() / helmet() in server.js
recommendation: Add helmet() and an explicit CORS allowlist; PayPal client_id is public by design but confirm no secret is ever exposed this way.

issue: Container runs as root (no USER directive) and EXPOSE/CMD run node as root; image also lacks a non-root user, increasing blast radius of any RCE
evidence: FROM node:18-alpine ... CMD ["node", "backend/server.js"]  // no USER node
recommendation: Add `USER node` (node images include a node user) and ensure uploads dir is writable by it; run as non-root.

issue: req.params.name used directly as an object key on parsed JSON (features[req.params.name]) and reflected into error messages; prototype-pollution-style keys (__proto__/constructor) and reflected input are low-risk here but uncontrolled
evidence: const feature = features[req.params.name] ... throw new Error(`Feature '${req.params.name}' not found`)
recommendation: Use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(features, name) / a Map; validate name against a whitelist regex before lookup and reflection.
